reason: Survives on wording; the year needs correcting. Fetched Gutenberg 4200 (the Wheatley text of the Mynors Bright transcription, George Bell). The quotation is verbatim as the last sentence of the diary, colon and exclamation mark included, dated May 31, 1669, and followed by END OF THE DIARY. But the editor’s preface to the volume that carries this entry reads First issue of this edition June, 1896. 1893 is the date of volume I, so the source line’s 1893 dates the wrong volume. Wheatley’s edition ran from 1893 to 1899. Publishability and the six-in-the-morning test are borderline, since he likens losing his sight to going into his grave, but it is a prayer of resignation and the famous closing of the work. Wheatley’s own preface notes that the fear of blindness was happily falsified. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Pepys 0 of 3, not banned. Diary is the right form. The source line leads with the name and has no dash.
